S-duality

Words: 18
String duality OurBigBook.com
An S-duality relates descriptions at different coupling strengths. In type IIB superstring theory, SL(2,Z) acts on the axion-dilaton and string charge doublets.

NS5-brane (TNS5​=(2π)5gs2​α′31​)

Words: 18
String theory OurBigBook.com
An NS5-brane has five spatial dimensions and is magnetically charged under the Neveu–Schwarz two-form. Its string-frame brane tension scales as gs−2​.

Fundamental string (TF1​=1/(2πα′))

Words: 25
String theory OurBigBook.com
A fundamental string is the perturbative string of a string-theory description. Its string tension is the displayed expression in the string metric. It couples to the Neveu–Schwarz two-form.

Hagedorn temperature (TH​=βH−1​)

Words: 273 Articles: 2
String theory OurBigBook.com
If a density of states has high-energy growth proportional to a power of energy times eβH​E, its canonical Boltzmann sum fails for β<βH​. The Hagedorn temperature is the corresponding threshold. The open bosonic string mass spectrum and large-level degeneracy of an open bosonic string give βH​=4πα′​ in units with Boltzmann's constant, the speed of light and Planck's constant set to one. Polynomial prefactors affect behavior at the threshold itself; the growth alone does not distinguish a limiting temperature from a phase transition.

Thermal winding instability of a closed bosonic string (mth2​=β2/(4π2α′2)−4/α′)

Words: 78
Hagedorn temperature OurBigBook.com
Euclidean finite temperature compactifies time to a circle of radius Rβ​=β/(2π). The string oscillator ground states with zero momentum number and winding w=±1 have the displayed mass from the bosonic string mass spectrum. They become massless at βH​=4πα′​ and tachyonic at higher temperature. This thermal winding mode diagnoses breakdown of the perturbative low-temperature string gas at the Hagedorn temperature. The endpoint and order of a transition require interactions and a suitable stable vacuum; the ordinary zero-winding bosonic tachyon is already unstable independently of this thermal threshold.

Finite canonical partition function at the bosonic Hagedorn threshold (Z1​(βH​)<∞butZ1​ is nonanalytic at βH​)

Words: 123
Hagedorn temperature OurBigBook.com
For a critical closed bosonic string in 25 noncompact spatial dimensions, the smoothed string oscillator rest-mass density behaves as ρ(M)∼CM−26eβH​M, with βH​=4πα′​. At large M, the centre-of-mass momentum integral of e−βM2+p2​ is asymptotic to (2πM/β)25/2e−βM, up to the convention for phase-space measure. Thus the high-mass tail of the one-string canonical partition function is proportional to ∫M0​∞​M−27/2e−(β−βH​)MdM. This converges at β=βH​ but fails for β<βH​. Expanding about the endpoint gives twelve finite derivatives and a nonanalytic term proportional to (β−βH​)25/2; the thirteenth derivative diverges. Consequently exponential state growth does not imply divergence of the partition function at the threshold itself. The discussion assumes the separate infrared instability of the bosonic tachyon has been regulated and does not claim a stable bosonic thermal vacuum.

Brane (p-brane)

Words: 722 Articles: 13
String theory OurBigBook.com
A brane is an extended object with p spatial dimensions. Its history is a (p+1)-dimensional worldvolume embedded in target spacetime. A point particle has p=0, a string has p=1, and a membrane has p=2. Geometric brane actions depend on the induced worldvolume metric; D-branes also carry open-string endpoint and gauge-field data.

Four-dimensional supermembrane

Words: 135 Articles: 1
Brane OurBigBook.com
The four-dimensional minimal supersymmetric membrane has embedding coordinates (Xm,θα) with four real odd components. Its area term uses the supertranslation-invariant superspace coframe, and a Wess-Zumino brane coupling integrates a superspace three-form potential with closed four-form curvature. Equal charge magnitude and tension permit kappa symmetry. After worldvolume reparametrization and kappa fixing, one transverse scalar and one three-dimensional Majorana fermion remain. This gives the long-wavelength description of the translation and fermion zero modes of a supersymmetric domain wall; it is distinct from restricting the eleven-dimensional M2-brane to a four-dimensional target.

Supermembrane closed four-form (G4​ ∝ iΠm∧Πn∧dθˉγmn​dθ)

Words: 59
Four-dimensional supermembrane OurBigBook.com
The four-dimensional membrane Fierz rearrangement identity (Cγmn​)(αβ​(Cγn)γδ)​=0 makes the displayed supertranslation-invariant four-form closed. It is locally the exterior derivative of a three-form potential, which can change by an exact form under target supersymmetry. Pulling the potential back to a closed worldvolume gives an invariant Wess-Zumino brane coupling. The charge magnitude and normalization of this form are fixed together by cancellation of the area variation under kappa symmetry.

Dirac membrane action (S=−T∫d3ξ−deth​)

Words: 55
Brane OurBigBook.com
A relativistic membrane sweeps out a three-dimensional worldvolume with induced worldvolume metric hij​=∂i​Xm∂j​Xnηmn​. Its leading geometric action is tension times its invariant volume. In static gauge in four-dimensional spacetime, one transverse field Y gives hij​=ηij​+∂i​Y∂j​Y, and the matrix determinant lemma gives S=−T∫1+∂i​Y∂iY​. Expanding supplies the translation-zero-mode kinetic term. A domain wall of finite thickness also has higher-curvature corrections outside the long-wavelength limit.

Wess-Zumino brane coupling (qTp​∫Σ​X∗Ap+1​)

Words: 240 Articles: 3
Brane OurBigBook.com
A charged brane couples to an appropriate differential-form gauge potential through its pullback. Under A↦A+dΛ, a closed worldvolume changes the action by a boundary term, by Stokes theorem. Reversing the brane charge reverses this coupling, which matters in probe-force and supersymmetry calculations.

Electric and magnetic dimensions of a form-coupled brane (pmagnetic​=d−pelectric​−4)

A scalar primary operator transforms without a spin rotation and is characterized by its scaling dimension. Conformal symmetry fixes its two- and three-point functions up to constants, while a four-point function can depend on conformal cross-ratios.

A conformal descendant is obtained by applying one or more translation generators to a conformal primary operator. Its scaling dimension exceeds that of the primary by a nonnegative integer.

Positivity of descendant norms constrains the scaling dimension of a primary operator. For a nonidentity scalar primary in d≥2, unitarity requires Δ≥(d−2)/2.

The state–operator correspondence maps a local operator of scaling dimension Δ to a state on Sd−1×R whose cylinder energy is Δ/r for sphere radius r.
State-operator correspondence for Virasoro primaries (∣O⟩=O(0)∣0⟩)
Words: 61
State–operator correspondence OurBigBook.com
For a primary operator, T(z)O(0)∼hO(0)/z2+∂O(0)/z. Taking the residue against zn+1 gives the weight for n=0, the derivative descendant for n=−1, and zero for every n>0. Conversely the absence of positive-mode actions excludes higher poles in this operator product and gives the primary transformation law. The antiholomorphic argument is identical. Thus primary states and primary operators correspond under radial quantization.

If the only light field in AdS4 is the graviton, the dual CFT3 spectrum begins with the vacuum at dimension zero, the spin-two stress tensor at dimension three, and its non-null level-one descendants of spins two and three at dimension four.

The AdS/CFT correspondence identifies a conformal field theory with quantum gravity on an asymptotically anti-de Sitter spacetime. Boundary sources couple to CFT operators and equal boundary values of bulk fields.

A Euclidean conformal transformation pulls the flat metric back to a position-dependent positive multiple of itself. Its infinitesimal generator obeys the conformal Killing equation.

At nonzero charge density, a translationally invariant holographic state has infinite D.C. conductivity because an electric field continuously injects conserved momentum. Momentum relaxation broadens the zero-frequency delta function and makes the D.C. value finite.
